questions.q: The most direct, measurable energy benefit of keeping a green roof is:
questions.n: The soil and plant layer cuts heat gain through the roof.

questions.q: Which of these is an architectural device for cutting solar heat gain?
questions.n: Louvers shade glazing and walls from direct sun.

questions.q: Warm to cool summers and severe winters below about −30 °C:
questions.n: The Köppen D group.

questions.q: Which insulation has little R-value of its own but works well in the tropics when it faces an air gap, blocking radiant heat?
questions.n: Foil's low emissivity works against radiation and needs an air space to function.

questions.q: In the Philippines, the rainy season usually runs:
questions.n: The southwest monsoon period.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the "3Rs"?
questions.n: The 3Rs are reduce, reuse, recycle.

questions.q: Deserts and steppes where moisture evaporates fast and rain is scarce:
questions.n: The Köppen B group.

questions.q: Channel lock and wiggle wire fasten film to the frame of:
questions.n: The wire snaps into the channel to clamp the film.

questions.q: Which is NOT a radon-resistant construction measure?
o: A gas-permeable gravel layer under the slab
questions.n: Vent dampers are HVAC devices, not soil-gas controls.

questions.q: Warm indoor air rising and escaping high while cooler air enters low is the:
questions.n: The density difference drives the flow.

questions.q: SBS in building health means:
questions.n: Symptoms tied to time spent in a building.

questions.q: The regular, long-term pattern of weather in a place is its:
questions.n: Weather is day-to-day; climate is the long average.

questions.q: Openings on opposite or adjacent walls so wind blows through the room give:
questions.n: Pressure difference drives air across the room.

questions.q: Hot and humid, every month above 18 °C, over about 1,500 mm of rain a year:
questions.n: The Köppen A group.

questions.q: Seasonal reversal of winds and rainfall caused by uneven heating of land and sea is a:
questions.n: Amihan and habagat are monsoons.

questions.q: Damp soil, clay and aggregate compacted in layers inside forms to make walls is:
questions.n: An ancient technique revived for its low embodied energy.

questions.q: The envelope material whose job is to slow heat flow is:
questions.n: Insulation adds thermal resistance.

questions.q: In the Köppen system, climates where elevation decides temperature and vegetation are:
questions.n: Mountain climates vary with altitude.

questions.q: VOC stands for:
questions.n: VOCs off-gas from paints and adhesives.

questions.q: Which green roof type puts more load on the structure?
questions.n: Intensive roofs have deep soil, trees and paving, so they are much heavier.

questions.q: Design that uses local climate, like sun, wind and shade, to stay comfortable with little mechanical energy is:
questions.n: UN-Habitat's definition of passive design.

questions.q: A thermal break in a building envelope exists to:
o: Interrupt heat conduction through conductive parts
questions.n: A thermal break puts a low-conductivity material in a conductive path such as a metal window frame.

questions.q: UN Sustainable Development Goal 1 is:
questions.n: SDG 2 is Zero Hunger; SDG 13 is Climate Action.

questions.q: Baguio's mean annual temperature is around:
questions.n: Baguio is roughly 8–10 °C cooler than the lowlands.

questions.q: To get hot air out of a room, the most effective move is:
o: An exhaust fan high on the ceiling
questions.n: Hot air rises, so extract it at the top.

questions.q: Philippine climate type with no dry season and a pronounced maximum rain from December to February:
questions.n: The eastern seaboard climate.

questions.q: Philippine climate type with rain spread fairly evenly through the year:
questions.n: No dry season and no pronounced peak.

questions.q: The cool, dry northeast monsoon (amihan) blows from about November to February. Which direction does it come from?
questions.n: Habagat is the southwest monsoon; amihan is the northeast.

questions.q: A poor exterior color for a sun-exposed firewall is:
questions.n: Dark colors absorb solar heat.

questions.q: Which finish material has the lowest embodied energy?
questions.n: Aluminum is the highest; fired clay is far lower.

questions.q: To encourage stack ventilation, a design adds:
o: A tall open atrium or shaft with high vents
questions.n: Warm air rises and escapes high, drawing fresh air in low.

questions.q: A west-facing building occupied through peak afternoon heat should block heat from coming in at all. Which property matters most?
questions.n: Resistance to heat flow (R-value) keeps heat out regardless of storage.

questions.q: For the best thermal insulation in a window, specify:
o: Double glazing with a sealed air or gas cavity
questions.n: The sealed cavity between panes slows conductive heat transfer.

questions.q: A desert-like site in Ilocos has hot days and cool nights. Which material property soaks up daytime heat and releases it after dark?
questions.n: Massive walls store heat and delay it, evening out the indoor swing.

questions.q: On a flat concrete roof, where does insulation do the most good for thermal bridging, waterproofing protection and slab temperature?
questions.n: Insulation above the slab keeps the whole structure on the stable side and shields the membrane.

questions.q: A daytime-only training building in humid, still Laguna must shed heat quickly after sunset. Which wall property is wanted?
questions.n: Lightweight walls don't store heat, so the interior cools fast.

questions.q: Under a tropical metal roof, the key passive move against radiant heat is:
o: Reflective foil with an air gap
questions.n: Foil plus an air space blocks radiant transfer into the ceiling.

questions.q: A material's ability to absorb and store heat, delaying peak loads, is its:
questions.n: Thermal mass damps and delays temperature swings.
